title: Asking Prices and Describing Objects
summary: Asking what something costs and describing color, size, and basic properties.
whyItMatters: Price questions and simple descriptions let you participate in a real shopping exchange even with limited German. You can identify an item, ask its cost, understand the answer, and clarify which color or size you mean.

mentalModel.title: Point, identify, ask
mentalModel.content: A basic shopping exchange has three moves: identify the object, make sure both people mean the same item, then ask the price.

mentalModel.title: Match kostet to one and kosten to many
mentalModel.content: Use 'kostet' for one item and 'kosten' for plural items: 'Wie viel kostet der Tisch?' but 'Wie viel kosten die Stühle?'

mentalModel.title: Describe with simple sein sentences
mentalModel.content: At A1, use 'sein' plus a property: 'Die Lampe ist weiß.' This avoids adjective-ending complexity while still communicating clearly.

ruleBlocks.title: Ask the price of one item
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Wie viel kostet ...?' with a singular noun: 'Wie viel kostet die Lampe?'

ruleBlocks.title: Ask the price of several items
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Wie viel kosten ...?' with a plural noun: 'Wie viel kosten die Stühle?'

ruleBlocks.title: Clarify which object you mean
ruleBlocks.content: Use a short description such as 'die schwarze Tasche' or point with 'dieser Tisch / diese Lampe / dieses Sofa' when needed.

ruleBlocks.title: React with a simple evaluation
ruleBlocks.content: Use 'Das ist billig', 'Das ist teuer', or 'Das ist okay' to respond to the price.

tables.title: Shopping Phrase Bank
rows: How much does the lamp cost?
How much do the chairs cost?

patterns: Der / Die / Das + noun + ist + property
sentenceStructure: Begin a price question with 'Wie viel'.
Use singular 'kostet' or plural 'kosten' to match the item.
Identify the product with its article and noun.
Describe it in a separate 'sein' sentence when clarity is more important than compact phrasing.

concepts: identify products by color, size, and condition

comparisons.summary: The theme lesson provides object names and properties. This lesson arranges them into a practical buyer-seller exchange.
Articles help identify the product and its number. The verb changes between singular 'kostet' and plural 'kosten'.

examples.de: A: Wie viel kostet die Lampe? B: Sie kostet 29 Euro.
examples.en: A: How much does the lamp cost? B: It costs 29 euros.

examples.de: A: Wie viel kosten die Stühle? B: Sie kosten zusammen 80 Euro.
examples.en: A: How much do the chairs cost? B: Together they cost 80 euros.

examples.de: A: Welche Tasche? B: Die kleine schwarze Tasche.
examples.en: A: Which bag? B: The small black bag.

examples.de: A: Das Sofa kostet 900 Euro. B: Das ist zu teuer.
examples.en: A: The sofa costs 900 euros. B: That is too expensive.

examples.de: Der Tisch ist groß, modern und günstig.
examples.en: The table is large, modern, and reasonably priced.

commonMistakes.reason: The plural subject 'die Stühle' requires the plural verb form 'kosten'.
Name or clearly identify the item whose price you are asking.
After a number, the German currency name normally remains 'Euro'.
After 'sein', use the basic adjective form without an article.

specialCases: 'Was kostet ...?' is also common and means the same as 'Wie viel kostet ...?' in a price question.
German decimal prices are written with a comma, for example '12,50 Euro'.
Demonstratives such as dieser, diese, and dieses are useful for pointing but change form with gender.
tips: Practice prices aloud with real products around you.
Always switch between one item and several items to train kostet versus kosten.
When adjective endings feel difficult, split the description into two sentences: 'Das ist eine Lampe. Die Lampe ist weiß.'

memoryHooks.title: One costs, many cost
memoryHooks.content: One item uses 'kostet'; several items use 'kosten'.

memoryHooks.title: Item, property, price
memoryHooks.content: Identify the object, clarify its visible property, then ask or state the price.
